readings.title: Moses Departs Midian
readings.subtitle: The Bridegroom of Blood
readings.text:
[Exodus 4:18] Then Mosheh went and returned to Yether his father-in-law, and said to him, “Please let me go and return to my brothers who are in Mitsrayim to see whether they are still alive.” And Yithro said to Mosheh, “Go in peace.”
[19] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh in Miḏyan, <dq>“Go, return to Mitsrayim, for all the men are dead who sought <dn>את</dn> your life.”</dq>
[20] So Mosheh took <dn>את</dn> his wife and <dn>את</dn> his sons and set them on a donkey, and he returned to the land of Mitsrayim. And Mosheh took <dn>את</dn> the rod of <dn>Elohim</dn> in his hand.
[21] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“As you go back to Mitsrayim, see that you do all those wonders before Pharaoh which <dn>I</dn> have put in your hand. But <dn>I</dn> am going to strengthen <dn>את</dn> his heart, so that he does not let <dn>את</dn> the people go.</dq>
[22] <dq>“And you shall say to Pharaoh, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Yisra’ěl is <dn>My</dn> son, <dn>My</dn> first-born,</dq>
[23] <dq>so <dn>I</dn> say to you, let <dn>My</dn> son go to serve <dn>Me</dn>. But if you refuse to let him go, see, <dn>I</dn> am killing <dn>את</dn> your son, your first-born.” ’ ”</dq>
[24] And it came to be on the way, in the lodging place, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> met him and sought to kill him.
[25] And Tsipporah took a sharp stone and cut off <dn>את</dn> the foreskin of her son and threw it at his feet, and said, “You are indeed a bridegroom of blood to me!”
[26] So <dn>He</dn> let him go. Then she said, “You are a bridegroom of blood,” because of the circumcision.
[27] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Aharon, <dq>“Go to meet Mosheh in the wilderness.”</dq> And he went and met him on the mountain of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and kissed him.
[28] Mosheh then told Aharon <dn>את</dn> all the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who had sent him, and <dn>את</dn> all the signs which <dn>He</dn> had commanded him.
[29] And Mosheh went with Aharon and gathered together <dn>את</dn> all the elders of the children of Yisra’ěl.
[30] And Aharon spoke <dn>את</dn> all the words which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had spoken to Mosheh. Then he did the signs before the eyes of the people.
[31] And the people believed. And they heard that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had visited <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl and that <dn>He</dn> had looked on <dn>את</dn> their affliction, and they bowed their heads and did obeisance.

readings.title: Let My People Go
readings.subtitle: Pharaoh's Refusal
readings.text:
[Exodus 5:1] And afterwards Mosheh and Aharon went in and said to Pharaoh, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘Let <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people go, so that they celebrate a festival to <dn>Me</dn> in the wilderness.’</dq> ”
[2] And Pharaoh said, “Who is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that I should obey <dn>His</dn> voice to let <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl go? I do not know <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, nor am I going to let <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl go.”
[3] And they said, “The <dn>Elohim</dn> of the Hebrews has met with us. Please, let us go three days’ journey into the wilderness and slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, lest <dn>He</dn> fall upon us with pestilence or with the sword.”
[4] But the sovereign of Mitsrayim said to them, “Mosheh and Aharon, why do you take <dn>את</dn> the people from their work? Get back to your burdens.”
[5] And Pharaoh said, “See, the people of the land are many now, and you make them cease from their burdens!”

readings.title: The Burden of Bricks Increased
readings.subtitle: The Foremen Cry Out
readings.text:
[Exodus 5:6] And the same day Pharaoh commanded <dn>את</dn> the slave-drivers of the people and <dn>את</dn> their foremen, saying,
[7] “You are no longer to give the people straw to make bricks as before. Let them go and gather straw for themselves.
[8] “And lay on them <dn>את</dn> the required amount of bricks which they made before, do not diminish it. For they are idle, that is why they cry out, saying, ‘Let us go and slaughter to our <dn>Elohim</dn>.’
[9] “Let more work be laid on the men, so that they labour in it, and not pay attention to words of falsehood.”
[10] And the slave-drivers of the people and their foremen went out and spoke to the people, saying, “Thus said Pharaoh, ‘I do not give you straw.
[11] ‘Go, take straw for yourselves, where ever you find it, for your work shall not be diminished.’ ”
[12] And the people were scattered in all the land of Mitsrayim – to gather stubble for straw.
[13] And the slave-drivers were hurrying them on, saying, “Fulfill your actions, your daily matters, as when there was straw.”
[14] Also the foremen of the children of Yisra’ěl, whom Pharaoh’s slave-drivers had set over them, were struck and were asked, “Why have you not fulfilled your law in making bricks both yesterday and today, as before?”
[15] And the foremen of the children of Yisra’ěl came and cried out to Pharaoh, saying, “Why do you treat your servants this way?
[16] “There is no straw given to your servants, and they say to us, ‘Make bricks!’ And see, your servants are struck, but your own people are at fault.”
[17] But he said, “You are idle! You are idle! That is why you say, ‘Let us go and slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’
[18] “So now go, work. And straw is not given to you, but deliver the amount of bricks.”
[19] And the foremen of the children of Yisra’ěl saw that they were in trouble after it was said, “You are not to diminish your daily amount of bricks.”
[20] And when they came out from Pharaoh, they met <dn>את</dn> Mosheh and <dn>את</dn> Aharon who stood there to meet them.
[21] And they said to them, “Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> look on you and judge, because you have made <dn>את</dn> us loathsome in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants, to give a sword in their hand to kill us.”
[22] And Mosheh returned to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, why have <dn>You</dn> done evil to this people? Why did <dn>You</dn> send me?
[23] “For ever since I came to Pharaoh to speak in <dn>Your</dn> Name, he has done evil to this people. And <dn>You</dn> have not delivered <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> people at all.”

readings.title: I Am YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: The Assurance to Moses
readings.text:
[Exodus 6:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Now see what <dn>I</dn> do to Pharaoh, for with a strong hand he is going to let them go, and with a strong hand he is going to drive them out of his land.”</dq>
[2] And <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke to Mosheh and said to him, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[3] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> appeared to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya‛aqoḇ, as <dn>Ěl</dn> Shaddai. And by <dn>My</dn> Name, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, was <dn>I</dn> not known to them?</dq>
[4] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> also established <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant with <dn>את</dn> them, to give them <dn>את</dn> the land of Kena‛an, <dn>את</dn> the land of their sojournings, in which they have sojourned.</dq>
[5] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> have also heard <dn>את</dn> the groaning of the children of Yisra’ěl whom the Mitsrites are enslaving, and <dn>I</dn> have remembered <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant.</dq>
[6] <dq>“Say, therefore, to the children of Yisra’ěl, ‘<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> shall bring you out from under the burdens of the Mitsrites, and shall deliver you from their enslaving, and shall redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with great judgments,</dq>
[7] <dq>and shall take you as <dn>My</dn> people, and <dn>I</dn> shall be your <dn>Elohim</dn>. And you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> who is bringing you out from under the burdens of the Mitsrites.</dq>
[8] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall bring you into the land which <dn>I</dn> swore to give to Aḇraham, to Yitsḥaq, and to Ya‛aqoḇ, to give it to you as an inheritance. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq>
[9] And Mosheh spoke thus to the children of Yisra’ěl, but they did not listen to Mosheh, because of shortness of spirit, and from hard slavery.
[10] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying,
[11] <dq>“Go in, speak to Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim, to let <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl go out of his land.”</dq>
[12] And Mosheh spoke before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “The children of Yisra’ěl have not listened to me, and why would Pharaoh listen to me, for I am of uncircumcised lips?”
[13] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, and gave them a command for the children of Yisra’ěl and for Pharaoh, sovereign of Mitsrayim, to bring <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl out of the land of Mitsrayim.

readings.section: The Genealogy of Moses and Aaron
readings.subsection: The Heads of the Fathers' Houses
readings.title: The Lineage of Levi
readings.subtitle: The Commission Repeated
readings.text:
[Exodus 6:14] These are the heads of their fathers’ houses: The sons of Re’uḇěn, the first-born of Yisra’ěl: Ḥanoḵ and Pallu, Ḥetsron and Karmi. These are the clans of Re’uḇěn.
[15] And the sons of Shim‛on: Yemu’ěl, and Yamin, and Ohaḏ, and Yaḵin, and Tsoḥar, and Sha’ul the son of a Kena‛anite woman. These are the clans of Shim‛on.
[16] These are the names of the sons of Lěvi according to their generations: Gěrshon, and Qehath, and Merari. And the years of the life of Lěvi were one hundred and thirty-seven.
[17] The sons of Gěrshon: Liḇni and Shim‛i according to their clans.
[18] And the sons of Qehath: Amram, and Yitshar, and Ḥeḇron, and Uzzi’ěl. And the years of the life of Qehath were one hundred and thirty-three.
[19] And the sons of Merari: Maḥli and Mushi. These are the clans of Lěvi according to their generations.
[20] And Amram took for himself <dn>את</dn> Yoḵeḇeḏ, his father’s sister, as wife. And she bore him <dn>את</dn> Aharon and <dn>את</dn> Mosheh. And the years of the life of Amram were one hundred and thirty-seven.
[21] And the sons of Yitshar: Qoraḥ, and Nepheḡ, and Ziḵri.
[22] And the sons of Uzzi’ěl: Misha’ěl, and Eltsaphan, and Sithri.
[23] Aharon took to himself <dn>את</dn> Elisheḇa, daughter of Amminaḏaḇ, sister of Naḥshon, as wife. And she bore him <dn>את</dn> Naḏaḇ, and <dn>את</dn> Aḇihu, <dn>את</dn> El‛azar, and <dn>את</dn> Ithamar.
[24] And the sons of Qoraḥ: Assir, Elqanah, and Aḇiyasaph. These are the clans of the Qorḥites.
[25] And El‛azar, Aharon’s son, took for himself one of the daughters of Puti’ěl as wife. And she bore him <dn>את</dn> Pineḥas. These are the heads of the fathers of the Lěvites according to their clans.
[26] This is Aharon, and Mosheh, to whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Bring out <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl from the land of Mitsrayim according to their divisions.”</dq>
[27] They were the ones who spoke to Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim, to bring out <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl from Mitsrayim. This is Mosheh, and Aharon.
[28] And it came to be, on the day when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh in the land of Mitsrayim,
[29] that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Speak to Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>I</dn> say to you.”</dq>
[30] And Mosheh said before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “See, I am of uncircumcised lips, and why would Pharaoh listen to me?”

readings.title: Moses as Elohim to Pharaoh
readings.subtitle: Aaron's Rod Becomes a Serpent
readings.text:
[Exodus 7:1] So <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> have made you an elohim to Pharaoh, and Aharon your brother is your prophet.</dq>
[2] <dq>“You shall speak <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>I</dn> command you, and Aharon your brother shall speak to Pharaoh, to let <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl go out of his land.</dq>
[3] <dq>“But <dn>I</dn> am going to harden <dn>את</dn> the heart of Pharaoh, and shall increase <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> signs and <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> wonders in the land of Mitsrayim.</dq>
[4] <dq>“And Pharaoh is not going to listen to you, and <dn>I</dn> shall lay <dn>My</dn> hand on Mitsrayim, and bring <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> divisions and <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people, the children of Yisra’ěl, out of the land of Mitsrayim by great judgments.</dq>
[5] <dq>“And the Mitsrites shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, when <dn>I</dn> stretch out <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> hand on Mitsrayim. And <dn>I</dn> shall bring <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl out from among them.”</dq>
[6] And Mosheh and Aharon did as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded them, so they did.
[7] Now Mosheh was eighty years old and Aharon eighty-three years old when they spoke to Pharaoh.
[8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying,
[9] <dq>“When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, ‘Show a miracle for yourselves,’ then you shall say to Aharon, ‘Take <dn>את</dn> your rod and throw it before Pharaoh, and let it become a serpent.’ ”</dq>
[10] So Mosheh and Aharon went in to Pharaoh, and they did so, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded. And Aharon threw <dn>את</dn> his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.
[11] But Pharaoh also called the wise men and the practisers of witchcraft. And they, the magicians of Mitsrayim, also did so with their magic.
[12] And they, each one, threw down his rod, and they became serpents. But the rod of Aharon swallowed up <dn>את</dn> their rods.
[13] And Pharaoh’s heart was strengthened, and he did not listen to them, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said.
